utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could the witness be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Berisha. May I remind you that the affirmation you made to tell the truth still applies. Yes, please, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Madam Berisha.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Excuse me. I would like to receive my interpretation in Albanian, not in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: On Monday, Madam Berisha, when you last testified, we spoke about the events on the 25th of March during the day after which your family and Faton's family moved into Vesel Berisha's house. Today I'd like to move on to the next day, the 26th of March, 1999; and I hope to go through your evidence fairly efficiently. Madam Berisha, on the 26th of March did you see any vehicles or equipment in the vicinity of Vesel Berisha's house?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 26th of March, above Uncle Vesel's house, there is a piece of land there, not arable land. It's a hilly place. And there were two large tanks placed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you recall what colour these tanks were?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I'm not quite certain. It could have been either dark blue or dark green. I don't remember it exactly, but I do remember that these two tanks were up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. On Monday you had mentioned seeing a tank in the vicinity of Agron Berisha's house. Can you remember how this tank behind Vesel's house was different from Agron's -- was different from the tank outside Agron's house?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tank in front of Agron's house, pointing at our house, was metal, was smaller in size, and he had -- it had wheels, while the two tanks above our two houses, they were larger in size, and they had tracks on them, not wheels.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And did these tanks have a gun or cannon on them?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The gun or cannon was pointing at our houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Berisha. On that day, on the 26th of March, what happened around mid-day?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At around noon, the police from the police station were large in number. They were dressed in uniforms. They were all carrying automatic rifles and they were moving around the houses. First, they set off in the direction of Ismet Kuci's house. There were not so many people there, so they didn't stay there for long. And then they ran in the direction of our house and came in our house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how many policemen there were?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were many, many policemen, a large group of policemen. There were also civilians, people not dressed in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And those who were dressed in uniforms, do you recall how their uniforms looked?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not very sure; however, they were uniforms of dark blue colour. But I don't remember it now clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You mentioned that these individuals ran in the direction of your house and came in -- came into your house. Did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Both Drilon and Sedat first recognised Zoran. I knew Zoran very well, too. He is a Serb who lived and worked in Suhareka, and he spoke Albanian very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to allow the witness to complete her sentence. This is examination-in-chief. The witness never said that the policemen entered the house, whereas my learned friend the Prosecutor is asking questions about what happened once they had entered the house. I believe we should allow the witness to tell us her story as it happened, and I don't think we should be asking her leading questions in the process. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you would take notice of that, please, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The policemen did not enter the house. When I gave my statement to the ICTY investigator, I made it clear that the policemen did not enter the house. They stayed outside in the yard. There was no reason for them to go inside. First of all, Zoran called for Bujar in Albanian, and when the men said it's better that we go out; otherwise, they're going to burn us alive inside, so we all - Children, women, men - ran outside and kept running. So they did not enter the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If I just may stop you there, Madam Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Perhaps there is an issue with the translation because the English transcript referred to the witness saying that the individuals came into the house, which is what I quoted later on. But now it appears that we have clarified the matter. But just for the record, I note that there may have been an issue with the translation in regard to that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The earlier evidence was that they had entered the house. You're quite correct in that matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, she said they came into the house. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Well, in any case, I will move on now Madam Berisha. You said that Zoran called out for Bujar in Albanian. And what happened after he called for Bujar?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he called out for Bujar, we were all very scared. Bujar's mother said that she would go out first. When she went outside, he was shouting at her and he said to her, Let Bujar come outside, not you. You go inside. And then Bujar went outside and asked Zoran what he wanted of him, and at that time, we heard gun-shots and we started running; and we left the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Berisha. How did you know that this individual who called for Bujar was Zoran?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew Zoran very well, and I saw him there amongst the group members, and I could tell it was Zoran because of his voice. He spoke Albanian very well, and he was the loudest of all in the group.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: In addition to calling out to Bujar, did Zoran say anything else?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He, he was cursing all the time. He was saying to us, Call on the Americans, your friends now, to help you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: What language was he speaking in, Madam Berisha?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zoran would sometimes speak in Serbian and sometimes in Albania. When I say "speak," I mean curse.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that after you heard gun-shots, that you started running out of the house. I'd like to clarify at this stage who else was in the house with you.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of us, the entire family. My family, my husband, my children, and Vjollca's family.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Perhaps to clarify, we could have a look at the Berisha family tree again. That would be Exhibit P272, and I believe I circulated hard copies to Your Honours and Defence counsel on Monday, but I do have a spare copy available for the witness. With Your Honours' leave, I'd like to pass it on to her.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So, Madam Berisha, when you say that those in the house were your entire family - your family, your husband, your children - and Vjollca's family, are you referring to the family tree at the top-most portion of the page, so the families of Faik and Bahrije and Vesel and Hava?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Were there any of those individuals who were not in the house that day?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that house the following persons were not there: The ones whose names are written in black letters. Naim, Vesel, Ismet, Arben, Faik and Bahrije. These were the persons who were not in the house. And the rest, all of us, about 24 or 25 members, were there in the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you started running out of the house. Did you see anyone while you were running out of the house?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Bujar went outside we started running. We left the house. I heard two gun-shots. And when I went outside I saw him, Bujar, lying on the balcony, and his wife then screamed, she said, Poor me, they killed my Bujar, and then we just ran as fast as we could. And when we got to our house, my house, there they had stopped my husband, Nexhat; Faton, his nephew; and Nexhmedin. Miskovic was holding Nexhat by his arm. Miskovic was a policeman from Suhareka whom I knew very well. He was not wearing a police uniform but he was wearing black clothes. There was another policeman whom I didn't know. He was also holding Faton by his arm. In the meantime, Faton's mother, Fatime, said to him, Take me instead of my son; just let him go. And at that moment Sedat started to run. He was trying to escape, but they caught him again, and I never saw Sedat again. He was trying to leave in the direction of Agron's house, but I never saw him again.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: What happened to your husband Nexhat, Madam Berisha, after they stopped him?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stopped there with my four children and with Vjollca's daughter, Dafina. I was holding Altin by his hand. Majlinda was carrying the younger son in her hands, and Herolinda was also with me. So we stopped there to see what they were going to do with the men. We were very scared. My children refused to continue walking. So he grabbed Nexhat by his arm and said to him, Now the Americans should come and rescue you, and he shot him on his back twice; and Nexhat fell on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: What happened to Nexhmedin, Madam Berisha?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nexhmedin, with his wife, were trying to escape. Lirija, similarly to Fatime, went to get Nexhmedin. She was Nexhmedin's wife. She was very young. She was pregnant. Her due date was two weeks later. But when the shooting got more intensive, and there were other voices speaking in Serbia telling them, Shoot, what are you waiting for? So when they were shooting from all sides, I just said to my children, Run because wear going to kill us, too. So Nexhmedin and Lirija were also running. Myself and Herolinda were running in one direction and Majlinda with my two sons, Altin and Redon as well as Vjollca's daughter, Dafina were running in the other direction. And I didn't -- I couldn't see any more what was going on there. It was terrible. There was a lot of shooting, a lot of shouting. We were just trying to escape.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Berisha. Do you know what happened to Faton?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is that I saw Faton and Fatime fall on the ground. I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You mentioned that you and your children started running in different directions. In which direction did you run?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: With my daughter Herolinda, we ran in the direction of the bus station, the petrol station. We were running very fast. A cousin of my husband, Jashar Berisha was there, and he asked me, What's going on? Why are you running? And I said to him, Uncle Jashar, they killed all our husbands, all our men, and we were trying to save our lives. And near the shopping centre we saw other members of our family, so with my daughter I joined them. I asked them, Why did you stop here? Nobody replied. And then a cousin of my husband said, The policemen told us to stop here. There were two Berisha families there in that location.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: What was the name of your husband's cousin who said the policemen asked you to stop at the coffee shop?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a cousin and best friend of my husband. We all called him Tushi. And if I'm not mistaken, his name was Avdi Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Who else was -- who else was gathered there, apart from Avdi and your family?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hajdin Berisha's family was there, so my family, Vjollca's family, Avdi Berisha's family, and another Berisha family.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, you said that Hajdin Berisha's family was there, Vjollca's family, Avdi Berisha's family, and another Berisha family. Please could you repeat the name of the last Berisha family?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hajdin Berisha's family.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vesel Berisha was Hajdin's father. Bujar's father, too, was called Vesel, so that's why I said Hajdin Berisha's family, to be more clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Again, just to clarify, perhaps we could have a look at the family tree again; that would be P272. And when you say the family of Avdi Berisha, am I correct that that is the family tree situated in the middle of the page?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Avdi Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And when you mention the Hajdin family and Vesel Berisha being his father, are you referring to the family tree right at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: After your family was gathered, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one particular moment my children came, and Altin said to me, Mommy, they injured me. Blood was coming out of his arm. And he said, Mommy, the police were shooting in my direction but they didn't quite hit me. He was pale. His heart was racing. They were shooting even at the children who were running away. Soon a group of policemen came and told us to go in. There was a cafe. There were tables inside, so we all went inside. They told us to sit down, and as soon as we sat, they started to shoot uninterruptedly. It was a burst of fire, automatic fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, can you describe the policemen to us?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them. I know it was a group of policemen, but nobody could see them, recognise them. It was a large number of people in one place. I just know that a group of policemen came and told us to go inside. And they were shouting, they were saying that they were going to kill all the Albanians, that they will not let a single Albanian live. But from the voice, it always looked to me that it was Zoran who was shouting the most.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Apart from the shooting, Madam Berisha, did you hear anything else?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, as I said, they opened fire, bursts of fire. Then they stopped. And as soon as they would notice that there were voices inside, people alive, then they were throwing things in and children, women, were just dying afterwards. It was sort of a grenade. As I said, I couldn't see. I was lying on the ground. I just could hear people crying, moaning, and after these things were thrown inside, it was just calm. They would not speak anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, what injuries, if any, did you sustain?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was inflicted many injuries. My whole body is covered with injuries. It goes by the Serb police when they hit at me, but God saved me to come here and tell the truth. When they saw that I was alive, they fired again on my arm. The bullet passed through my arm, but I still remained alive, even though they thought that I was dead because they didn't -- they thought that everybody was dead. But I feigned I was dead. They thought I was dead; that's why they stopped firing at me. I have wounds all over my body, where the shrapnel hit me in my leg, on my chest, on my stomach. All over my body, even today I have many shrapnels inside my body.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, when the shooting stopped, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the shooting stopped, and when they did short work of almost everyone -- now it's very difficult indeed for me to mention them by name, they spoke in Serbian, Let us load the bodies in the truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these voices?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I did not, because I didn't raise my head up. I feigned death, as I said, but I heard them speaking among themselves in Serbian, one of them saying, What life is this? Why are they killing women and children? The other one rhetorically, Let's go and clean everything. There were two persons, and they conversed in Serbian between themselves. And then they had a stretcher and they carried the corpses. Some were still alive. Drilon was still alive. But when they saw that someone was alive, they fired again, and the woman or the child died. This was the case with my son, too, who was first wounded. He also was wounded in the leg. Gramoz was also wounded. They didn't see Gramoz because his face was covered with the jacket. My Altin was still alive. I said to him, Mom, pretend you are dead. He didn't make any sound, but they noticed he was alive when they raised his body and then they fired again, and I heard only a moan. Then they started to transport all the corpses. They did the same with me. I had two golden chains around my neck, but to them those chains seemed to be more precious than my life. They unclasped them, and they took them away from me. For me, of course, they had no value, but this is just to show you what they did. They took away the chains and threw me on the truck --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And what happened --

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and all my family was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And what happened once you were loaded onto the truck, Madam Berisha?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After they loaded us onto the truck, there was a stench coming from all over the place. There was blood all over. There were about 40 people. The truck started to move a while and then stopped. When it stopped, a woman spoke in Serbian, saying -- saying, My son, are you finished? He said, Yes, we are finished. And then they said, Have a good trip. And then I lifted my head and Vjollca did the same. And I was looking at my son Altin to see whether he was alive. I started to speak to him. Vjollca heard me speaking to Altin and she asked me, Are you still alive? And I said, Yes, I am still alive, but they have killed all our kinfolk. The Serb police killed every one of our families. This was before the truck stopped. Then it stopped, and that woman spoke in Serbian. And it seemed to me that she was Zoran's mother, even though I didn't see her. But from the voice I think it was Zoran's mother. Then I said to Vjollca, Did you hear Vera of Laza, what she said of Zoran, Did you finish the job? She said yes, because she knew Vera of Laza better than me. After that the truck continued on it's way --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, may I just stop you there. When you referred to Vera of Laza, was that also a reference to Zoran's mother, the woman you referring to earlier who spoke Serbian?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Berisha. Before we move on to what happened once you were loaded onto the truck and the truck started to move, perhaps we could have a look at Exhibit 272 again, which is your family tree. Amongst all the names in blue listed on that page, Madam Berisha, who survived the incident at the cafe?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The names in blue and the other names, they were all there. Of all of them only myself, Vjollca, and Gramoz were alive. The others were killed, even though, as I said, some of them were still alive when they loaded us onto the truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: How old was Gramoz at that time, Madam Berisha?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eight years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eight years and a half, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could I call up Exhibit P269, page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Before we move on, Madam Berisha, I wonder if you could please identify on this map the location of the cafe that you referred to as being the site of the incident you just testified about.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately here is the gas station, in this part here. Somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could you mark it with a number 1, please.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain that this is exactly the place because I have forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That's absolutely fine. But you recall that it was thereabouts?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify the marking that you made, is that the gas station or the cafe?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The gas station is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness said she could not say where the coffee bar was. She said she was unable to say. She marked the approximate area where the coffee bar was, so why insist on a precise location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The question was directed to something a little different, I think, Mr. Djurdjic, whether being marked was the position of the petrol station, which had been mentioned by the witness, or the cafe; and it was that ambiguity which was being clarified, as I understand it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, just to clarify, the marking that you made at number 1, what location was that? What building?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: My hand was shaking. This is where the cafe is, but as I said, I cannot concentrate on the exact spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: But not here. On this other side here, the cafe is here.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Is that where the number 1 is placed, where you placed the number 1?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies matters. Thank you very much. I will move on now, Madam Berisha, and I hope to go through the next parts fairly -- fairly quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you proposing to tender this?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, please, Your Honours. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00275, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, after you were loaded onto the truck, what happened?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Together with Vjollca, we were very scared and very worried and upset. We started to talk with one another. She said, Gramoz is alive, and that she had thought that Nexhat was injured. But maybe when Lirija came to call us, to call Nexhmedin and Nexhat, maybe someone had helped him. I said, Let us jump from the truck because I don't want to surrender to the Serbs, to these wretched Serbs who killed our kids. Let us jump down and tell who killed us. Then Vjollca said, No, Shyhrete, we cannot jump from the truck. But when they cover us, when they bury us, then we'll try and come out of the earth. I said, No, we cannot do that. And then I saw that there was a curtain covering, like a plastic curtain covering the truck, a tarpaulin covering the truck, and I saw a hole there. I didn't know where we were. I said, Vjollca -- she was on the edge of the truck. She said, Don't try to jump from the sides because they can see us in the mirrors. And she said, Better jump from the end side, the rear, because they won't see us. The truck was driving fast and then when I -- as I was talking with Vjollca, I jumped down, and when I fell down, I hurt my forehead. There was a great wound, a lot of blood. Then after, awhile Vjollca and Gramoz jumped, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, do you recall where you jumped off?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After I fell down some people helped me. It is Malasia e Re, a village in the direction of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: What happened after these people helped you? What did they do?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A girl saw me and she called her father, and that old man called two young men, telling them to go and pick up a wounded woman who was covered in blood all over. Two young men came and picked me up and took me to a house. They started to give me the first aid. They took me to Grejkoc village. There was a doctor there, but they were not in a position to give me a great help.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Kosovo after this incident, Madam Berisha?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed until May. Then I went to a village, Budakova, it's called. There I met my parents who learned what had happened to our family, because what happened was known to the Serbs in Mushtisht. People talked about what happened, what the Serbs did, what the police did to children and to women. So my father had gotten wind of what happened and both of them came to the village. There is a forest nearby. We met together, and I joined them with my uncles in Vranig . We stayed there all the time in the mountain, even though I was full of wounds. One day, I became very sad because many children died in the forest. Some girls got mad. They couldn't take it any longer. So the men decided that we have to surrender. We were with our tractors. They said, If they are going to kill us, let them kill us, all of us, because we can't take this situation anymore. So the man showed a white sheet and then the convoy of tractors and cars started to move. When we came to Bukosh village, there was great confusion there. For me it was a very difficult day. It was like the same day they killed my kids. I couldn't take the chaos, the tumult, people all over, the police, armed police coming there shouting and shooting. They took the man, the young man, some young men, my uncle, too; and they took some women to a school nearby, robbing them of everybody precious they had, and they returned the women but not some of the men. Those men never returned. Their bodies were discovered after the war. Some other older men, my uncle one of them, they were released. They returned to the group and then we went to another village. So this is how we started our way, our trip towards Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, where did you cross into Albania, at which border crossing, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Kukes, but I'm not certain about the date, whether it was the 5th or the 6th of May. I only know that it was early May.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And what happened at the Kukes border crossing?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the Kukes border crossing, the police were very aggressive towards us. They were dressed in uniforms. I couldn't stand them any more. I couldn't stand the arms. They said to us that, We will kill all of you. A woman fainted. The police approached her and said, She's good for nothing. Some women threw water over her face, and she regained her consciousness. They asked us to give them money and our IDs. Also there was great confusion. Most of us were women, girls, children; and all of us were very scared. But we passed that and then we -- that phase and then we entered Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that you were asked to give your IDs. Were they returned to you?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Whoever had the IDs on them, they surrendered them, but they were not given back to them, at least I don't know. I didn't have mine. But I saw many other women who submitted their IDs to the police but they were not returned to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, once you crossed into Albania, did you provide the ICTY with a blood sample?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Djurdjic, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Berisha, my name is Veljko Djurdjic. I'm a member of Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic's Defence team. I'm joined here today by Ms. Marie O'Leary, another member of the Defence team. Mr. Dragoljub Djordjevic, who is normally with us and lead counsel for Mr. Djordjevic, is today absent. Before I start with my questions, I would like to express my most sincere condolences to you, and Mr. Djordjevic, on account of what happened to your nearest and dearest. Originally, I was not going to ask you any questions about the subject of your evidence here, but I find myself unable to avoid the issue generally. I will be skirting the issue in a manner of speaking, but I do have to ask you some questions related to the overall context. In your statements, you say that you completed a degree of higher schooling, as I put it, but I couldn't quite conclude what that might be. Can you be more specific about that? What exactly? Where and when?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I finished the high school in Suhareka, whereas the higher pedagogical studies in Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And what year was that, the Prizren school? When did you complete your education there?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1981. I'm not certain. I have forgotten because you have destroyed my memory. I can't give you exact dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Ms. Berisha. Was that a mixed school in terms of ethnicities? Was it attended by all the various ethnicities from the area?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember about the higher pedagogical school, but in the high school, yes, we were of various ethnicities together, both Albanians and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that after school you did not get a job?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true. After school I didn't work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Berisha, could you tell me about your husband Nexhat, about his educational background?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nexhat finished high school and started his studies in the faculty in Prishtina, but he didn't continue it. So he found a job in the hall of culture of Suhareka, responsible for amateur activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about 1998 and 1999, did he continue to work in the culture hall throughout those two years?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He didn't work in the last years because he was dismissed from work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm looking at your evidence in the Milutinovic case. You say that your husband went to the OSCE building on a daily basis. Was he, in fact, an employee of the OSCE in 1998 -- in late 1998 and early 1999?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, he was not an employee of the OSCE, but he simply went there every day. He had the right to go to his own house whenever he wished.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what he did when he went there, since your part of the house was attached to the offices, as you suggested?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first my husband and my two daughters went there to clean the house for awhile, but then the OSCE hired a maid. So my husband went there every day to Suhareka. The kids were there in school, so my husband went there every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe I understood you correctly, and please correct me if I am wrong, did your husband move to your father's place later on with you?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we started to rent our house to the OSCE, the OSCE staff came to our house and myself, my children, and myself went to Mushtisht and that's where we lived, slept. But my three children, Majlinda, Altin, and Herolinda, continued their school in Suhareka; so they travelled every day from Mushtisht to Suhareka, and so did my husband. He travelled with my father's car on a daily basis to Suhareka. My children would go to school sometimes by bus and sometimes by car with my husband. But my husband, as I said, was not employed with the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Berisha, would you agree with me that the new house which you built is on Miladin Popovic Street, which people normally refer to as Restanski Pot?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me when you built this new house, and when it was eventually moved in?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This house was built for several years. It was built slowly; the construction took some years. But myself, I lived there for a year only.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated in your evidence that in the ground floor of that new house, there was a shop selling spare parts for cars; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a small shop selling spare parts for cars, yes. This was on Faton's side of the house, not on our side of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Correct me if I'm wrong, was that shop actually owned by Faton?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Faton's property.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I, therefore, conclude that you never went to that shop? Answer please.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You nodded but we need a verbal answer from you. That is why I asked you to please answer. Just for the sake of the record, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I conclude that you never entered that shop, did you? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did go to this shop, of course, before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you go into the shop after you had returned, following the 20th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 20th of March, no. No, I didn't enter the shop after that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would I be right to claim that you don't know what was actually in that shop, or you didn't know what was there when you returned to your home in March?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know very well what was in there. There were spare parts for cars, and the same person who worked there at the time is working there now. There was nothing else but spare parts for cars, sir. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who owned the shop, really?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same owner who owned this shop during the war, he still owns this shop. But it will take me a few minutes to remember his name. I know him. I cannot recall his name for the moment. His wife is employed in Balkans. She's a cousin of mine. This person, this man who owns the shop is from Sematisht, the village, and his brother-in-law works in that shop. These people were there until a year ago or so. I used to see them after the war. I don't know if they are still there, but I know that they continued their business with this shop, with spare parts for cars, even after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 6th of March, was anyone manning the shop that morning?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of March?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, on the 26th of March.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody was there. Nobody was working there on the 26th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Shyhrete, when did you find out that the OSCE had arrived in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The OSCE arrived in the Suhareka area in 1998. I don't know the exact date, but I know that it came in the Suhareka area in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is this something you heard from someone or did you actually see them?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them myself. The OSCE was staying in the Boss Hotel in Shirokq. This is a village that I pass by every time I visit my parents. So I visited my parents very often, so I saw the OSCE people and the OSCE vehicles at this hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated in chief that your husband and Faton met the people who were working for the OSCE. Can you tell us when, where, and how they met?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The OSCE people came to our house. I was there with my children when they came to our house. And they asked my husband and Faton whether they would agree to rent the house to them. So my husband and Faton agreed, and this is how they came to stay in our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Berisha, you said that while driving to Musutiste with your husband, you passed the Boss Hotel. Your husband pointed out to you the person, whose last name you said was Miskovic; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't my husband who pointed him to me. I knew Miskovic myself. He was a policeman in Suhareka. Everybody new Miskovic in Suhareka.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see the contract between your husband, I assume, and the OSCE on the lease?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the contract, and I was there when they made this agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Berisha, are you certain that it was, in fact, a contract with the OSCE and not some other group of observers, a mission?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I'm sure this contract was entered with OSCE members. The boss, the chief of the OSCE was an American. He was a tall man called Rufus. At that time, I knew his full name, but now ten years have passed and I don't remember his full name. So when I arrived in Albania, Rufus was there. He was the first to meet me there in Albania. And he felt for myself and my whole family, for the men of my family because they were young and intellectuals; and they were people who would never have done something similar to what the Serbs did to our family. So I'm more than sure that this contract was made with the OSCE people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Will you take my word for it if I tell you that at the Boss Hotel, that what was there was the Kosovo Diplomatic Mission. It wasn't the OSCE who were staying at the Boss Hotel back in 1998.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe you, because the truth is that the OSCE was staying in the Boss Hotel, in Shirokq. Miskovic's brother worked there as a guard, security guard, and he also came to our house when the OSCE moved to our house to work as a security guard. The OSCE, as I said, I'm sure, was in Shirokq, in the Boss Hotel, and from there they moved to our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How come you know that Miskovic's brother was working there as a guard, I mean at the Boss Hotel?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know this because my elder daughter, Majlinda, once told me that Miskovic's brother, who worked as a security guard for the OSCE in the Boss Hotel, was also working as a security guard with the OSCE now in our house. And I also remember my husband telling me the same thing when he came to the house to ask about the copier, photocopying machine. So I know this, and I'm sure about this. This is true, that Miskovic's brother worked as a security guard in our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: May I, therefore, conclude that you do not in any direct knowledge of this? You only know as much as you were told by your husband and your daughter.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That you, yourself, never saw Miskovic's brother working as a guard at the Boss Hotel while the mission was staying there.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see Miskovic's brother at the Boss Hotel, but I did see him with my own eyes when he worked as a security guard in our house. I often visited Vjollca in her house with my younger son, when my husband was not at home, so I saw Miskovic's brother with my own eyes working there as a security guard. And when they surrounded our house and killed us all, Miskovic was there. He took part in those events. But he, as I said, was not wearing a uniform on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Ms. Shyhrete, can you please answer my question and nothing but my question? My question was about the guard duty or the security at the Boss Hotel. I did not ask you about anything else. In order to speed things along, and in order to remain focused, please try to answer only the questions that I actually ask you. Thank you. Ms. Berisha, you told us that on the morning of the 25th, at 5.00 as a matter of fact, someone knocked on the door in that part of the house in which you were staying. You went there and you opened the door for them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Ms. Shyhrete, I have been to many Albanian homes, country-side and town alike. I have never, ever seen a lady or even a child open the door. Is it really part of the tradition cherished by the Albanians for wives and ladies in the house to go and open a door when a guest arrives, particularly a guest arriving at 5.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't a guest because this was war time. And the family I was married in, the men and the women were equal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, 5.00 a.m., I don't think that could be defined as a welcomed guest.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What does that have to do with anything? Of course it wasn't a welcomed guest. I was very sure that it was the police at that door because there was shooting. And for the whole day I was scared, and I feared that they, the Serb police, would come to our house, the same thing they did with other houses where the OSCE used to stay. I was not an illiterate woman. I had the right to open the door of my house, to go wherever I wanted. I enjoyed all the rights as a woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that you found policemen outside the door the morning of the 25th. That's the time that I mean. Can you please describe their uniforms.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all dressed in uniforms and carrying automatic rifles. As I said, ten years have passed now, and I cannot give you the details; I cannot tell the colours. But they were all dressed in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you conclude that they were policemen?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were dressed in uniforms. They were armed with automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, were there any other uniformed formations carrying the same kind of weapon?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people were wearing uniforms and carrying automatic rifles. I have nothing else to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My question following your previous answer was, how did you conclude or what led you to conclude that those persons were police officers?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they were not dressed in civilian clothes; they were wearing uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could we perhaps conclude that the only thing you are certain about is the fact that at the door the persons standing there were uniformed, carrying weapons. That's all you're certain about, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not about being certain. This is something that I've seen with my own eyes, and I'm a person who has gone through a lot. They were speaking in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that you did not go to the part of your house in which your husband was staying, with the police?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The police prevented me from doing that. As soon as they would notice me as I was trying to look in that direction, they would shout at me and tell me to go inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that in Faton's part of the house, which is where you went to next, there was a uniformed person who came in with you?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Faton's part of the house, a policeman came in. He was dressed in uniform. He started to search the cupboards, the wardrobes, and I spoke to him in Serbian. I said to him, There's nothing here; only children's clothes. And as I said earlier, he found a bag, he searched the bag, and when he saw that there was nothing in it, money or gold, jewelry, he just threw the bag away. On the staircase there was some medicine for the children in there. So he said for me to follow him down to the basement. He made the money sign with his finger. He asked me for money and said to me, You know that your husband's life is in danger. So I went upstairs and took 1.000 DM from Sebahate. And when he looked at the money he said, This is not enough for your husband's life. And I just said to him that I had no more money with me, and he left the house and went outside in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that your husband went back with the policemen to the part of the house in which you were staying with Faton's family?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the policemen brought my husband there, and at the door-step they hit him with the rifle and kicked him. He fell right there on the door-step, but he stood up and came inside the house together with these three policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it not true that you said that the policemen had asked for money to spare your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's working now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient moment, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the policemen --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have another question, but we might as well break. I do think it might be better to finish this particular set of questions, but it's up to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Finish now this bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Have you perhaps forgotten my last question, Ms. Shyhrete? Should I repeat it for you?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The policemen, one of the policemen asked for money to save my husband's life, because his life was in danger, as he said. But those other policemen who brought my husband to the house, they also asked for money. They said to us, See that tank up there? We will burn you all, and we will blow this house up in the air with all the children in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Ms. Shyhrete, did you give 3.000 marks to the policemen to stop them from killing your husband?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had 3.000 DM in me, and I gave them to the policemen. First of all, I gave 1.000 DM to the policeman in the basement who told me that my husband's life was in danger, but these other three policemen were different, not the same with that one. So I gave these other three policemen 3.000 Deutschemarks that I had in me. I was just too scared. I thought that they were going to undress me, so I just took the money out and gave them the money.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You were concealing this money in your bra; am I right?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my body, on my body.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My last question, Ms. Berisha: The first time the policemen came you went to Sebahate and you got 1.000 Deutschemarks in order to give the policeman in order to stop him from killing your husband; and yet now you tell us that you had 3.000 Deutschemarks on you, whereas you had told the first policeman that you had no more money, so you gave him the 1.000 German marks that Sebahate had given you.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I told the policeman that I didn't have any money. I went upstairs to the room and I took 1.000 DM from Sebahate. I was only -- it was only me and this policeman in the basement, so I didn't dare to take this money from my body. If I tried to take it out of my body, I feared that something might have -- might happen to me. That's why I said to this policeman, Wait here. I'll check with the women upstairs, if they have any money. So I took this 1.000 Deutschemarks from Sebahate and returned to the basement and gave him the 1.000, but those 3.000 that were on my body were still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I then conclude that the policeman was in the basement while you walked up to the second floor and then back down?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He remained in the basement. I went upstairs, took 1.000 DM, and brought him this amount in the basement. But he wanted more, but I just said to him that I didn't have any money, other money, with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have a break now. We will resume at 20 minutes after 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Shyhrete, on the 25th of March when you moved from the Faton part of the house to the house of Vesel Berisha ...

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 25th of March, after the Serb police took our money and other things they wanted from the house, they took the tank that was pointing to our house, and we were very scared. We stayed a little while and then went to Uncle Vesel's house, and we got together as a family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think there's something wrong with the interpretation. My question was when, on the 25th of March, 1999, did they go from Faton's part of the house to the house of Vesel Berisha.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us that, Ms. Berisha, when it was that you went?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we went to Vesel's house after the Serb police left our home, but I am not sure about the exact time. Maybe after two hours or three hours; this I cannot tell you for sure. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Berisha, yesterday you indicated the Pristina-Prizren road on the photograph. That's where you saw the columns of police and military vehicles. What house were you in at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time we were at Faton's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You marked the position and you spoke about the tank that was on the road. Did you notice when that tank left and where it went?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tank left from Faton's house and went in the direction of the police station. I don't know more after that. I only know that it headed towards the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That morning at 5.00 a.m., did you see police and military columns, convoys, passing by your house towards the village of Rastane.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I know only what I saw happening in our yard. When they threw all over papers, the tank was there. They left with the tank. All this I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Madam, that morning did you hear tanks passing by in front of your house? Did you hear buses and military trucks passing by and going off in the direction of Rastane? I'm referring to the morning of the 25th.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anything coming from Rrashtan, going towards Rrashtan. I saw buses, tanks, trucks, passing by the direction of Prishtina or by the direction of Prizren only.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have Exhibit P269 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Shyhrete, could you please mark with a number 1 the house where you were on the 25th of March, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the morning of the 25th of March, I was in our own part of the house -- correction, in Faton's part of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please now mark with a number 2 the Suva Reka police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm afraid we appear to have lost number 1, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In this photograph can we see the house of Hajdin Berisha?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it can be seen, but I'm not sure whether it's this one here. I'm not certain because I didn't know well which house belonged to whom. Somewhere here. I know that these group of houses belonged to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you circle that group of houses, the approximate location where you think Hajdin Berisha was?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hajdin's house is approximately here. These are Hajdin's, Avdiu, my husband's cousins' houses; but I didn't know exactly which belonged to whom, as I side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you please put a circle around the group of houses where you think Hajdin's house was, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not certain of them. I already said, I knew the people but I didn't know very well whose houses were where. But approximately, the houses were here. I'm not certain which belonged to Hajdin or to his brother. I'm not certain because even at that time I said that I don't know exactly which house belongs to whom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: When you say there that you think his house was in a group here, could you put a circle around that position? We understand you've made it clear that you don't know exactly which was his house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not certain. I believe it was this one because I never was in his house. I only know that they were close to our house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps you can mark that with a number 3, if you could, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That may help, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Berisha, let's clarify a point. I think you said that a year before the OSCE arrived you moved into that house. Did you know the area and your neighbourhood very well? Were you familiar with it? Did you know where people lived and where their houses were?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I knew the place where my house was and the houses of the close relatives of my husband. These two were cousins of my husband but a little bit more removed. They belonged to another branch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, Mrs. Berisha. I do apologise, but please listen to my questions carefully so that we can move forward faster and avoid wasting time. There are lots of houses here, and the Berisha family is perhaps the biggest in Suva Reka. We see dozens of houses here. What I was asking you was did you know the people in the neighbourhood well? Because if you didn't, I'm don't want waste time trying to get you to indicate houses that you don't know the location of, because you had only been living there for a relatively short time, about a year, and you see how many houses there are here.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lived there for about a year, but my husband's cousins, the ones who live here --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There was something else I wanted to ask you now, because you spoke about this yesterday. But in this house do you know where the carpenter's shop is, in Miladin Popovic Street or, rather, on the Ristane road?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can we see the Muslim cemetery here or the road leading up to it?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The road that leads to the cemetery is on this side. I don't know if you can see it. I don't know. I don't see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see the turning? You can see the main road, but do you see the turning? So can you draw an arrow showing the road leading to the Muslim cemetery, if you can see it.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain whether it's here, this turning, or here. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Approximately --

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I didn't go to the cemetery very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you draw an arrow indicating the direction so that we know more or less where it is?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot, because I said I don't know, I'm not sure. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Shyhrete. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to tender this exhibit into evidence. May it be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00020, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to have P269 brought up on the screen again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Berisha, could you put a number 1 on Vesel Berisha's house.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And could you please mark with a number 2 the house of Ismet Kuci.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about Ismet Kuci's house either. I can't see it very well. I'm not sure whether this is his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What house are you referring to? Can you mark it with an X, if you're not sure?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure of Ismet Kuci's house. I cannot concentrate and find it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And could you please mark with the number 3 the police station, the Suva Reka OUP.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you now mark the place where you first saw policemen on that morning, the 26th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The place where we saw the policemen is here, in this direction. We saw them running.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you place an X on the place where you first saw policemen on the 26th of March, 1999, in the morning, where you, yourself, saw them?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the police station, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please mark the line along which they moved. Draw a line along the direction they were moving in.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Of course only what you saw yourself.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a group of policemen and they spread out in different directions. Some came to us, some here, some here, so in many directions there were running policemen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I mention for the transcript that the witness first drew an arrow from what appears to be the police building across the street with an arrow-head on it, as the position where police were first seen; and then has now marked four further lines spreading out from that first marking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Shyhrete, you told us today and more than once in your statements that policemen entered the house of Ismet Kuci. Can you now recall where Ismet Kuci's house is?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These houses here, these houses here, but I am not certain now. From the police station they ran and came in these directions. They didn't run all in one direction. As I said, there were many people running in different directions. Some came towards Ismet Kuci's house; some others, a little bit further, and so on, in all directions. It was a fighting. It's the Serb police that kept running and running. Even in the movies you wouldn't see such a kind of organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Ms. Shyhrete, you told us both today and several times before that you saw policemen entering Ismet Kuci's house, and since it was empty they left very soon after that and went to your house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan, before you answer, please, Ms. Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Djurdjic could point to the transcript reference where the witness said that they entered Ismet Kuci's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My learned friend today, when you started asking questions about the 26th of March, the witness said they entered Ismet Kuci's house, but because it was empty, they left it very soon thereafter and then arrived at the house where the witness was. And now my colleague will find the transcript reference; however, I think you remember putting the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I do, and the reference that I have is at page 2, line 20, which reads that: "First they set off in the direction of Ismet Kuci's house. There were not so many people there so they didn't stay there for long." I'm unable to locate a reference to them entering Ismet Kuci's house. Perhaps counsel could assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: As they didn't find many people there, they went on. That's an even better reference than mine.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't find anyone. There wasn't anyone at all in Ismet Kuci's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Shyhrete. I don't want to maltreat you, but I think it's important for you to indicate Ismet Kuci's house if you can. If you can't, tell us so and we will move on. Let's move on. Could you please mark the place on Vesel Berisha's house where you were while you were observing all this, all the things you have told us about, seeing the policemen and so on?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were here, from this entrance. As I said, the house has two entrances, but you can enter it from four sides. Two are up, and two are a little bit lower. We were here, at a lower plain. This is the entrance. This is the window. There is a window here, and then there is the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now mark the door through which you ran out of the house?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The door is here in front, but the house is shown on the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you please, Ms. Berisha, mark with a number 4 the position from which you saw the police. You've put two dots on the building and you've told us it was there and at that lower level of the building. If you could put a 4 against that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Not the upper entrances, because there is a flight of steps and there is the entrance, but this other entrance a little bit lower.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Can you put a 4 to the left of what you have just marked, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm afraid the number 4 has merged in with the other markings that were already there. It's a bit difficult to identify the number 4. Could you do something different for me: Mark with the number 5 the position of the doorway from which you left the building, as you've described.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's rather difficult here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you put the number 5 out in the garden, outside the doorway perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise, I think that the next photograph we see will probably be better for marking that gate, that doorway, and then we can mark that there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I mention, Mr. Djurdjic, that it is very difficult in my experience here for witnesses who are seeing an aerial photograph for the very first time often to recognise a building or a location, because they have spent their life looking at it from ground level, not from an aeroplane, and it does look very different. So we may be spending a lot of time and not getting very far in pursuing this line. I leave it now to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this exhibit please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00021, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now if I could have D9 displayed, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Madam, do you recognise the area as seen from this angle and the location of your home?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us about the position of those two tanks near your house, if you can actually see their positions in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see them. They would be much higher up, up higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Madam, may I therefore conclude that the tank was on Dulje, up a hill, that that's where it was, and that's where you saw it?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No, it wasn't in Dula. You couldn't have seen it from there. It was just above the house. There are fields there, and it was a little bit above that. There are a few trees there and that's where the tanks were, the two tanks were positioned. But it's not Dula at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now we see Vesel Berisha's house clearly, although we've never actually looked at it from this angle, and that probably includes you, as well. Can we here see the gate from which you came running at the time, or was it on the other side?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entrance is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about the basement from which you ran out? Where exactly was that?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sitting room was over here where we were, but it's not in the basement. It's on the main floor. And the floor above that is here, but we were on the main floor. It's not in the basement. There was no basement at that time. We were in the sitting room, the living room.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Fine. I'm sorry if I made a mistake. Can you please mark the room in which you were before you ran out of the house.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same room here, the one here which has its entrance here. It's a large room, and the door is over here, and there's a window. That is the living room.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm looking now at your statement dated the 15th of May, 1999. I would like to read a portion to you. You said: "All men and children went down to the basement of the house."

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a ground-floor room, and it was used like a sort of basement. Sometimes we call it a living room, but we also call it a basement because it was on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Fine. We'll get back to that later for other reasons. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not sure if we should have this admitted as well, since the witness marked the entrance and the location of the room which they were before they ran out of the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will receive this photograph. The blue marking shows the position indicated by the witness of the doorway from which they came.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00022, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Madam, on the 26th of March, 1999, when you saw the policemen near the police station heading for your homes, what sort of uniforms were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, many years have passed, and I'm not too sure about the colour of the uniforms, but they all had the same uniforms. And they were wearing caps and had automatic rifles over their -- in their arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the main road, the Pristina-Prizren road, near the police station? Did you see any lorries there on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the 26th of March?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right. I apologise. The 26th of March, that's the only date I'm discussing.

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 26th, when we left the house with Vjollca, we left Agron's house and front of -- over there, there was a truck, a large truck parked; and below that there was a large man standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Madam, I'm asking you about that morning when you saw the policemen near the police station. What about the Prizren-Pristina road just across the way from the police station in Suva Reka? Did you see two lorries there, parked there?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Parked lorries we saw only in front of the house, in front of our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the junction, the Rastane road and the Pristina-Prizren main road, the intersection? Did you see a jeep that we parked there when you were inside the house looking towards the police station?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The moment we left the house, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, madam. When you were inside the house looking towards the policemen leaving the police station, did you see a jeep parked at the very intersection of the main road and your own street?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the police went to our house in the morning, there was a column of vehicles, of police vehicles. I didn't see any particular jeeps, but there were trucks parked in front of our house at the moment we were leaving. And there were also jeeps and buses and trucks around before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Madam, we are talking about a truck that was parked outside the shop selling spare parts for cars; am I right?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the truck was in front of the house when we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam, do you remember your evidence before the war crimes district court in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: SHYHRETE BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
